Does Home Field Still Matter?
NFL home-field advantage · every game, 1920 –

Does home field still matter?

The edge, season by season

Each point is one season. The adjusted measure subtracts the strength gap between the two teams, estimated each season from every score, so a home edge cannot come from good teams happening to host more games. The dashed line marks the bettor's old rule of thumb: home field is worth 3 points.

By Super Bowl era

The first Super Bowl followed the 1966 season. Before it, the NFL, AFL and AAFC crowned champions without one. The Super Bowl years split into stretches defined by schedule length and how teams were built: the AFL–NFL years and 14-game seasons, the 16-game schedule before the salary cap, the salary-cap and free-agency years, the 2020 season played mostly without fans, and the 17-game schedule. Each row uses the filters set in the season chart.

What moves the edge

Strength-adjusted home edge in points, with 95% intervals, split by the conditions of the game. The split uses whatever filters are set above (except the one being split on). A bar crossing zero means that slice gives the home team no measurable help.

The regressions

Game-level OLS of the home team's point margin, standard errors clustered by season. The venue model starts in 1966, the first year with stadium and weather records; football-specific stadiums are the reference group for stadium type.

Franchises: names, cities, and records

Pick a franchise to see its colors, every name and city it has used, its home and road record, and its edge decade by decade.

Stadiums

Every venue used as a home field since 1966, with surface history, roof, stadium type and baseball tenancy. Oakland, San Francisco, Pittsburgh, Philadelphia, Cincinnati and others shared with MLB teams; early-season games there were often played across the baseball infield dirt. Click a column to sort.

Data and method

  • Games. 1920–1998 from FiveThirtyEight's NFL Elo game archive (includes AFL and AAFC); 1999– from nflverse schedules, which carry ESPN game IDs, stadium, roof, surface, temperature, wind and the closing point spread. The two sources agree on the 1999–2020 overlap (home win rate 57.05% vs 57.06%).
  • Stadiums and weather, 1966–1998. Venue and kickoff weather from the NFLweather-derived "spreadspoke" scores file, matched to 99% of games. Surface history, roof, stadium type, baseball tenancy and approximate capacity are compiled by hand from stadium histories. Games before 1966 have no stadium record; all were outdoors on grass.
  • Attendance. Per-game home attendance exists only for 2000–2019 in the open data used here. The 2020 season, played mostly without fans, stands in for the zero-attendance case.
  • Strength adjustment. For each season a least-squares rating is fit for every team together with a single home-field term (margin = home edge + ratinghome − ratingaway), with light shrinkage. The adjusted margin of a game is its margin minus the rating gap. Neutral-site games serve as a placebo: their adjusted "home" margin is .
  • Baseball-configured fields. A game is flagged when the stadium had an MLB co-tenant that year and kickoff fell before October 4, when the infield was usually still dirt.
  • Not done. ESPN, the Weather Channel and Pro-Football-Reference could not be reached for bulk download, so stadium shape is a category rather than a measured geometry, and pre-1966 weather is absent. Travel distance, time zones and rest days are not modeled.

Sources

  • FiveThirtyEight, nfl-elo-game: every game 1920–2020, scores and neutral/playoff flags (file data/nfl_games.csv). Used for 1920–1998.
  • nflverse, nfldata: every game 1999–2026 with ESPN game IDs, stadium, roof, surface, temperature, wind, spread (file data/games.csv).
  • NFL scores and betting data ("spreadspoke"), Kaggle: stadium and kickoff weather 1966–2025; copy downloaded from the lillyjob/nfl-spread-dashboard GitHub mirror.
  • TidyTuesday 2020-02-04, NFL attendance: weekly attendance by team, 2000–2019.
  • ESPN: game pages linked from the game finder for 1999+ (via nflverse ESPN IDs).
  • Stadium surface checks: Wikipedia, Tulane Stadium, FirstBank (Vanderbilt) Stadium, RFK Stadium. Remaining venue history compiled from public stadium records.
  • Team colors: each franchise's official primary and secondary colors, shown as badges (no logos).
